title: DeepSeek's V4 Pro API model quietly updated to an 0813 version
reason: Surfaced via Simon Willison's Weblog (tier 3, discovery only): the deepseek-v4-pro API alias was silently repointed to an 0813-dated version, no dedicated changelog or announcement page found on DeepSeek's own site -- confirmed only via a footnote on the 'Your First API Call' docs page ('the deepseek-v4-pro model has been updated to DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813'). No open-weights repo for this version found on huggingface.co/deepseek-ai as of this check (only DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark and DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark listed, all July or earlier). dedup-check: zero matches against the existing deepseek-v4-flash-0731-beta article (that story covered the Flash variant only). Residual-substance test not yet clearable: no stated changelog, no benchmark claims, no confirmation of what changed technically or whether weights will be released -- there is a version-bump fact but no article-worthy claim set yet. Held rather than rushed given this cycle's tight time budget; would need either an official DeepSeek changelog entry or a substantive third-party diff (benchmark delta, capability change) to clear the bar.
watch: A DeepSeek News (api-docs.deepseek.com/news) entry or updates-log line describing what changed in the 0813 version
Open-weights release of DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 on Hugging Face
Independent benchmark delta versus the prior V4-Pro (DSpark) version
notes: 2026-08-13 c4: opened as watching-only; not run through full verify/falsify given thin substance and cycle time budget. Revisit in a later cycle's triage if fresh evidence appears.

No DeepSeek changelog entry found. Gate still fails on substance. Still watching.

2026-08-14 c1: Re-checked (1 web search). Substance has grown: multiple outlets (TechTimes, GMI Cloud, Unite.AI, digitalapplied, Simon Willison) now report the 0813 build left API preview on 2026-08-12 and cite specific benchmark deltas vendor-reported by DeepSeek versus the preview build (DeepSWE 12.8 to 62.7, CyberGym 52.7 to 83.3, Terminal Bench 2.1 72.1 to 87.9). TechTimes' own headline frames these as awaiting independent proof -- still vendor-sourced, no independent benchmark run (METR, Vals AI, Artificial Analysis) yet, still no DeepSeek changelog or blog entry, only the pricing-page and API behavior change. Residual-substance test is closer to clearing (real shipped model, real vendor benchmark numbers) but would need labeling as vendor-claim plus a dedicated verify pass this entry has not had. No open-weights release found. Gate still fails pending independent confirmation or a full verify pass. Still watching.

2026-08-13 c2 (23:03Z ingest): Story has materially changed shape -- this is no longer just a quiet API repoint. Reuters (via TradingView reprint) and Nikkei Asia both report DeepSeek's own on-the-record announcement that V4-Pro-0813 formally exits preview today (2026-08-13), available across app/web/API, with DeepSeek itself stating the release focuses on agent capabilities (tool use, code execution, multi-step workflows) and confirming a specific price change (V4-Pro output tokens to $3.96/M at peak from a flat $0.87/M). This is now a company-confirmed product launch (not an unnamed-sources claim) covered independently by two tier-0/1 outlets, which clears the sourcing/independence bar for the *launch and pricing* facts. The vendor benchmark-delta claims (DeepSWE/CyberGym/Terminal Bench) remain unconfirmed by any independent evaluator and would need separate labeling as vendor-reported if used. Did NOT run this cycle's full verify+adversarial-falsify+bilingual write+editor-gate protocol -- cycle had a ~28-minute window (23:03-23:32 UTC) after the mandatory discovery sweep and no time to safely complete it. Flagging as highest-priority pickup for the next cycle: launch+pricing facts look publication-ready pending the standard verify/falsify pass; benchmark deltas should be labeled vendor-claim or omitted. Still watching.
